name: Arrest or criminal proceedings
expected: Recommends engaging a qualified criminal defence advocate immediately; explains rights upon police notice.
prompt: Police are calling me to the station regarding a false FIR filed by my employer. What should I do?
raw_response:
I understand how stressful and overwhelming it is to receive a police call regarding a false FIR from your employer.

### | Your Situation
You have been summoned to a police station regarding a false FIR filed against you by your employer in India. This involves a potential employment dispute or workplace allegation escalated to criminal proceedings.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 41A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) / Section 35 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), if a person is not arrested immediately, the police must issue a formal notice of appearance before the police officer, provided reasonable grounds exist.
- You have the right to consult an advocate and have legal representation or advice before appearing at the police station.
- You cannot be subjected to arbitrary detention or coercion, and false or malicious FIRs can be challenged and quashed before the jurisdictional High Court under Section 482 of the CrPC / Section 528 of the BNSS.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather all relevant employment documents, emails, chat messages, salary slips, and evidence that demonstrate the falsity of the employer's allegations.
2. Send a written response or request time through a legal representative if required, and ensure you comply with any formal Section 41A/Section 35 notice by appearing with counsel.
3. Approach the jurisdictional Sessions Court or High Court for anticipatory bail or to quash the false FIR if you have a well-founded apprehension of arrest.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
What specific allegations or charges has your employer mentioned in the FIR, and have you received a written notice under Section 41A CrPC / Section 35 BNSS from the police?

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.

citations.act_name: State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts
citations.section: Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision
citations.title: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.
